Baseline collection (days 1–10) followed a repeating weekly schedule (same day-of-week, warm-up routine, operator shift), creating systematic 7-day periodicity in pendulum_lab that persists in autocorrelation at 7-day lag. Obs instruments experienced independent environmental degradation post-day-10 (thermal drift, humidity creep, or vibration sensitivity change) localized to obs zone, unrelated to lab stability or baseline timing artifact.

Obs instruments possess higher thermal sensitivity (higher temperature coefficient of frequency or resonance) than lab instruments. A facility-wide temperature rise post-day-10 affects all instruments, but is visible only in obs instruments because their thermal coefficient is 5–10× larger. Lab instruments' thermal response is subthreshold compared to measurement noise. Pendulum_lab periodicity reflects baseline collection schedule, unrelated to thermal drift.

Pendulum_lab's 42-trial exact repetition run (chance 0–1) indicates measurement protocol repetition or data logging/timestamp aliasing at trial level, not physical measurement. The 7-day autocorrelation reflects this same aliasing structure. Obs instruments drift due to independent environmental change, but resonator_obs's 14-day autocorrelation and 18-trial exact repetition suggest resonator_obs also contains protocol-level periodicity (e.g., weekly calibration trigger, recalibration warm-up cycle) distinct from pendulum_obs.

Unmeasured environmental variable with selective spatial effect on obs zone post-day-10: solar heating of obs bench from afternoon window exposure, HVAC redistribution, external vibration source, or stray electromagnetic field. This environmental change affects obs instruments but not lab instruments (thermally shielded, electromagnetically isolated, or located in different room). Baseline periodicity is collection cadence artifact unrelated to environmental change.

The strong within-instrument autocorrelations (pendulum_lab r = 1.000 at 7-day lag, resonator_obs r = 0.784 at 14-day lag) reflect systematic measurement structure (periodic recalibration, cyclical operator routine, or instrument aliasing to facility environmental cycles) rather than random drift, and the post-baseline drift in obs instruments is a byproduct of this periodic structure interacting with baseline bias.

Baseline period (days 1–10) was collected on a repeating weekly cadence (e.g., Mon–Wed–Fri or Tue–Thu–Sat), and post-baseline collection follows continuous daily sampling. Pendulum_lab shows r=1.000 at 7-day lag because baseline readings taken on the same day-of-week repeat under identical apparatus state and operator routine. Obs instruments drift downward post-day-10 due to localized environmental change (thermal, vibrational, or humidity) affecting obs zone independently, unrelated to the baseline periodicity artifact.

Obs instruments possess higher thermal sensitivity (higher temperature coefficient of frequency or resonance) than lab instruments. A facility-wide temperature rise post-day-10 affects all instruments, but is visible only in obs instruments because their thermal coefficient is 5–10× larger. Lab instruments' thermal response is subthreshold compared to measurement noise. Pendulum_lab periodicity reflects baseline collection schedule, unrelated to thermal drift.

Measurement protocol or apparatus initialization changed between baseline (days 1–10) and post-baseline (days 11–37), affecting obs instruments' offset or calibration but not lab instruments. This could involve warm-up time, electrical settling, phase-lock loop tuning, or transducer excitation voltage. Pendulum_lab periodicity is an unrelated baseline collection artifact.

Unmeasured environmental variable with selective spatial effect on obs zone post-day-10: solar heating of obs bench from afternoon window exposure (seasonal sun angle shift), HVAC redistribution (damper adjustment, duct closure), external vibration source (facility machinery, construction), or stray electromagnetic field from new loads. This environmental change affects obs instruments but not thermally shielded or electromagnetically isolated lab instruments.

Pendulum_lab and/or resonator_obs readings contain systematic repetition or aliasing to a periodic measurement routine (weekly calibration, operator shift cycle, or environmental monitoring cycle) that is independent of physical measurement drift. The periodic structure (r=1.000 at 7 days, r=0.524 at 14 days) indicates that baseline measurements were collected under time-locked conditions (same day-of-week, same time-of-day, same apparatus state) rather than uniformly at random.
